action: Monex or SBI Shinsei customers: wait for the individual notice, watch for phishing that uses your email address or identity documents, and report any misuse to the firm.
date_note: Date SBI Shinsei Bank announced its customers may be affected; Monex's interim findings were published on 13 November and the intrusion attempt was detected on 18 October.
exec: A broker's account-opening system, run by a contractor, may have exposed up to 1.13 million email addresses and identity documents for 1,592 applications.
geo_basis: operator country (Japan); city not stated in the source
plain: Monex Securities said its online account-opening system may have leaked data, and SBI Shinsei Bank said its customers using Monex's intermediary service may be among those affected.
summary: According to Cybersecurity.com, Monex Securities said an external contractor's account-opening system detected an intrusion attempt on 18 October. Monex says up to 1.13 million email addresses entered since 16 October 2019 (including duplicates and unfinished applications) and identity-document images for 1,592 applications may have leaked. SBI Shinsei Bank announced on 18 November that its customers using Monex's intermediary service may be affected; it has not given a number.
title: SBI Shinsei Bank says customers may be affected by possible data leak at Monex Securities account-opening system

validation.note: Cybersecurity.com article read, relaying SBI Shinsei's and Monex's notices; the notices themselves were not read directly.

review.note: Title said 'breach'; sources say data may have leaked after an intrusion attempt. Figures 1.13M (up to, duplicates), 1,592, dates and SBI no-number checked OK
